messages.content:
You are verifying one structured PFAS study evidence record against the
complete source evidence cited by that record.

You receive:
1. the review task and task-specific extraction objective;
2. the held-out anchor identifiers;
3. one extracted evidence record; and
4. the complete source chunks or inspected source-page text referenced by the
   record.

Judge only source support and transcription. Do not reward usefulness,
verbosity, or agreement with general background knowledge.

Assess every substantive populated source-dependent field against only its
attached field-level locators. Do not create separate assessments for locator
arrays, record IDs, or formatting metadata:
- supported: the cited evidence directly supports the field and its material
  qualifiers;
- partially_supported: the core statement is supported but a material
  qualifier, condition, denominator, or scope is missing;
- unsupported: the cited evidence does not establish the field;
- contradicted: the cited evidence directly conflicts with the field.

For quantitative_findings, value must contain an actual number, censored or
approximate number, range, or explicit ND/not-detected result. A unit-shaped
string such as "nmol/L" in value with an empty unit is a unit error even when
the source mentions that concentration scale. Do not silently reinterpret one
schema field as another. Confirm that value matches value_form; explanatory
text and uncertainty belong in qualifiers.

Classify endpoint_type from the measured basis, not the source's terminology.
Parent-compound loss alone is not destruction; phase transfer is not
degradation; inorganic fluoride release or fluorine-balance closure establishes
defluorination but not mineralization. Mineralization requires direct
carbon-fate evidence such as measured CO2/inorganic carbon or a carbon balance.
If an author calls defluorination mineralization without that evidence, retain
the author phrase only as reported_term and mark endpoint_type=mineralization
unsupported with error_type=endpoint_classification.

Comparability is an analyst-derived judgment. Do not require the source to
state the comparability conclusion verbatim. Instead, judge whether its status
and reason follow conservatively from supported cited fields for matrix, PFAS
scope, scale, conditions, endpoint, unit, and denominator.

An author_reported limitation requires direct source support. A
design_inferred limitation is supported when it follows necessarily from
cited design facts; absence from the supplied packet is not a study
limitation.

Classify errors as numeric_transcription, unit, qualifier,
endpoint_classification, source_attribution, other, or none. A record is usable
only if its source identity, matrix, treatment, endpoints, and quantitative
findings are not unsupported or contradicted in a way that would mislead
  synthesis. A usable record can still contain non-core fields that synthesis
must exclude according to their field assessments.

For metric consistency, always emit separate assessments with these exact
field-path forms when the corresponding item exists:
- `quantitative_findings[i].value`;
- `quantitative_findings[i].unit`;
- `operating_conditions[i].value`;
- `operating_conditions[i].unit`;
- `endpoints[i].endpoint_type`; and
- `comparability.status`.

Other substantive fields may be assessed individually or as a whole object,
but do not omit these required assessment types and do not emit a required
field path more than once.

Report anchor_exclusion_violation=true if the source resolves to any held-out
anchor DOI, URL, exact title, or corpus source.

Return one JSON object that follows the supplied verification schema exactly.

field_assessments.reason: The DOI and URL exactly match the citation information in the provided source text.
Author list, year, article title, journal, volume, and article number all match the source citation.
Locator S08-E05 states that a CCMS was operated for treatment of an AFFF-impacted groundwater, matching the recorded matrix description.
S08-E05 describes a pilot demonstration and S08-E08 describes a closed-circuit membrane system (CCMS), supporting the description of a pilot-scale CCMS treating AFFF-impacted groundwater.
The work is explicitly described as a pilot demonstration (S08-E05), which aligns with the classification as pilot_or_field_deployment.
S08-E01 specifies a tight NF (NF90-4040, DuPont/FilmTec) membrane with a polyamide thin-film composite active layer, used in a CCMS, consistent with the treatment description.
S08-E01 identifies NF90-4040 as a tight NF membrane from DuPont/FilmTec with a polyamide thin-film composite active layer, matching the stated membrane type and properties.
No numeric value is given so the null unit is appropriate; the source simply specifies the membrane model and material without units.

S08-E01 and S08-E08 together describe a closed-circuit membrane system (CCMS) with retentate recycle, operated in recirculation with a subsequent plug-flow flush sequence, matching the recorded configuration.
This is a descriptive configuration with no numeric value, so a null unit is appropriate.
S08-E01 states that sulfuric acid was continuously dosed to reduce the feed pH to ~6.4, matching the recorded value and qualifier.
The pH is reported as a dimensionless value; leaving the unit null is appropriate and consistent with the source.
S08-E01 notes that a small volume (~20 μL) of Vitec 3000 antiscalant was dosed at the beginning of each sequence, matching the description.
This condition is descriptive (chemical and dosing description) and not a standalone numeric metric, so the null unit is appropriate.
S08-E05 states that the CCMS was operated at 80 %, 85 %, and 90 % system recoveries; summarizing this as 80-90 is faithful to the source values.
System recovery is expressed as percent in S08-E05, so the unit % is correct.
S08-E01 specifies that the SCADA system controlled operational conditions to ensure a constant system flux, matching the recorded description of flux control.
The condition is qualitative (constant flux control) without a numeric magnitude; a null unit is appropriate.

S08-E04 reports that the tight NF membrane (NF90) exhibited a lower NDP and higher TCSF than the brackish water RO (BW30) and more consistent average TCSF, which matches the recorded permeability indicator.
This is a qualitative comparative statement about TCSF and NDP without a specific numeric value; null unit is appropriate.

S08-E07 lists the PFAS classes as C4–C7 PFCAs, C5–C8 PFSAs, C4 and C6 FASAs, and C6 and C8 FTSs, which supports most of the description. However, the mention that these are in groundwater and that PFOS was 'specifically highlighted' is not directly stated in the provided locator text.
S08-E03 reports PFAS rejection percentages by NF and RO, which corresponds to a separation/removal endpoint.

S08-E03 states that rejection by NF ranged from 97.9 to 99.8 % and that it was impacted by functional group (carboxylates > sulfonates, fluorotelomer sulfonates > sulfonamides) and increased with chain length, matching the functional-group and chain-length description. However, the statement that this occurred 'across multiple PFAS classes in AFFF-impacted groundwater' oversteps what is explicitly in the cited abstract chunk, which does not mention the matrix or enumerate classes.
S08-E04 describes comparison of membrane operating performance using NDP, TCSF, and energy use rather than a direct separation metric, fitting an 'other' endpoint classification.

S08-E04 supports that NF90 had lower NDP, higher TCSF, and more consistent TCSF than BW30, and that these metrics were used alongside energy use. The added inference that this indicates 'lower pressure/energy demand for similar PFAS separation' extends beyond the explicit statements about energy in the provided text.
S08-E03 reports that 'Rejection by NF ranged from 97.9 to 99.8 %', matching the recorded range 97.9-99.8 with value_form = range.
The abstract in S08-E03 explicitly states the rejection range in percent, so the unit '%' is correct.

S08-E05 describes a single AFFF-impacted groundwater treated in a CCMS at pilot scale with two membranes, and S08-E01 specifies one tight NF model (NF90-4040). The limitation that results may not generalize to other waters, PFAS mixtures, or membrane products reasonably follows as a design-inferred limitation.

The study directly compares NF90 and BW30 membranes in the same CCMS treating the same AFFF-impacted groundwater at matched recoveries (80, 85, 90 %) with common endpoints (PFAS rejection, NDP, TCSF, energy), per S08-E03, S08-E04, and S08-E05. This supports that the systems are comparable with conditions.

S08-E05 specifies operation of a CCMS at 80–90 % recoveries with both membranes; S08-E03 and S08-E04 show direct comparison of PFAS rejection and operating metrics. The provided reason accurately reflects these conditions and metrics.

result.record_usable_rationale: Core elements—source identity, matrix, membrane type, treatment configuration, operating conditions, PFAS scope (classes), and quantitative PFAS rejection—are well supported by the cited text. Minor over-interpretations in endpoint interpretations and PFAS scope qualifiers do not affect the usability of the record for comparative membrane-performance synthesis.
